display_title: Adversarial Monte Carlo COA Analysis: Common Random Numbers, Ranking-and-Selection, and History-Matching Calibration (notional parameters)
one_liner: A terrain-aware stochastic combat simulation (company team to brigade) wrapped in a full simulation-analysis toolkit: paired COA comparison with CRN, Kim-Nelson selection, GP and Sobol sensitivity, and rung-by-rung history-matching calibration. The parameters are notional: the model is verified but not validated.
problem: Comparing courses of action with a stochastic combat model is only useful if the comparison is statistically honest (paired, interval-bounded, selection-bias-aware), the discretization is checked, and the parameters have a defined path from notional to calibrated.
approach: An entity engine runs on OSM or DEM or synthetic ground: detection hazard, multinomial-logit target choice, circular-normal hit probability, suppression, and Beta breakpoints. It uses named random substreams so COAs share random numbers. Around it sit Wilson/delta/sup-t intervals, Kaplan-Meier and Aalen-Johansen for censored outcomes, Kim-Nelson ranking-and-selection, a Latin hypercube design with a stochastic-kriging GP and Saltelli/Jansen Sobol indices, and history matching (implausibility, NROY waves) with a held-out terrain coverage check. An aggregate brigade engine is derived as a mean-field limit of the entity kill chain and bias-corrected against it.
decision_relevance: Supports COA analysis (which Blue scheme of maneuver is best, with what confidence) and shows the V&V and calibration process that Army analytic organizations apply to combat models. The outputs are methodological, not operational, because every parameter is notional.

headline_results.claim: Core mechanics and estimators are unit-tested: the hit-probability formula matches brute force, Wilson coverage holds, Kim-Nelson selects the known best system, and history matching retains a synthetic truth. 31 of 46 tests were rerun and passed.
headline_results.evidence: pytest tests/test_stats.py tests/test_sim.py tests/test_calibration.py: 31 passed in 74 s (2026-09-17 audit rerun)

headline_results.claim: Tick-length convergence: a 15 s tick is not converged (P(win) 0.565 -> 0.698 at 7.5 s), while 7.5 s and 3.75 s agree (0.698 vs 0.702) on the 25 m demo ground
headline_results.evidence: scripts/convergence.py --reps 1500 rerun at HEAD a20b7c9, seed 7

headline_results.claim: Rung-1 sensitivity: the GP metamodel is trusted (LOO R2 0.75-0.86, MC noise share 0.04-0.05); AT-team P_K dominates every output (total Sobol index 0.61-0.79)
The aggregate brigade engine, corrected against the entity engine, cuts the P(win) gap from +0.41 to +0.05 and loss-fraction gaps to about 0.01 (multipliers 0.63 / 2.54)
headline_results.evidence: data/aggregation_correction.json (residuals); raw gap from scripts/aggregation_check.py --raw, not rerun

headline_results.claim: The history-matching pipeline recovers hidden synthetic parameters and achieves 0.90 held-out coverage of 90% prediction intervals (31 outputs)

limitations: All parameters, nation catalogs and C2 profiles are notional. There is no validation against real engagements or a higher-fidelity model; every calibration uses the engine's own synthetic reference.
Intervals cover Monte Carlo error only, not model error. Parameter uncertainty was about 96% of outcome variance in the predecessor notebook.
Grid cell size is not converged on the demo ground: P(win) differs by 0.14-0.17 between 25 m and 12.5 m cells at fine ticks (audit rerun). The README currently says about 0.05.
Choice-model parameters (lam_blue, lam_red, b_threat) are not identifiable from aggregate outcomes.
The rung-5 aggregation correction is fitted at company scale and extrapolated to brigades.
Red is largely static in the entity engine. The brigade engine has no EW, fixed-wing air, or air-defence units.
Brigade results are quoted at n = 20 without intervals.
blockers_before_featuring: README section 10 convergence table (12.5 m rows) does not reproduce at HEAD with the fixed seed (rerun 0.236/0.401/0.529/0.567 vs stated 0.261/0.487/0.621/0.655), and the 'cell size matters about 0.05' finding is contradicted (actual 0.14-0.17). Regenerate, commit the JSON and manifest, and revise the finding.

Replace the 'Mathematically rigorous combat simulation' repo description with a method-first title plus 'notional parameters; verified, not validated'. Do not describe the attrition model as Lanchester (there is none; the aggregate engine is a mean-field kill-chain limit).
